title: Client backoff profiling and idempotency grace periods for tool invocations
author: Mira Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see applications that either (a) retry aggressively after partial stream interruptions and silently double-invoke downstream tools, or (b) apply overly conservative backoff parameters because there is no client-visible signal about recent request congestion. This PR introduces a pair of pragmatic, low-risk changes to improve client behavior: 1) a lightweight, machine-readable sampling hint (Retry-Sample) emitted by the gateway to help clients profile effective backoff windows for a route; and 2) a short-lived soft-idempotency session (Idempotency-Grace) for tool/function invocations to accept safe replays in the immediate aftermath of interrupted streams.

Summary of changes and rationale:
- New response header `Retry-Sample`: contains a compact comma-separated sample of recent effective backoff windows (ms) and an epoch timestamp (example: "1700000000:50,100,250"). The intent is for SDKs to record these samples and automatically adjust initial retry jitter/backoff distributions per-route instead of using static heuristics. This is an advisory, rate-limited signal (gateway emits at most one sample per route per 30s) and carries no permission semantics.
- New request/response handshake header `Idempotency-Grace`: when a tool invocation begins, the gateway creates a short-lived soft session (default TTL 30s) and returns an opaque session id in Idempotency-Grace. If the client observes a truncated stream or connection reset, it may retry the same invocation providing the session id; the runtime will treat the retry as non-duplicative if the session is still valid and the prior invocation did not persist side-effects. This dramatically reduces client-side forced throttling for transient network issues while preserving safety for persisted operations.
- Runtime implementation: an in-memory bounded soft session cache with LRU eviction plus a pluggable persistent backend used by Dedicated/Private deployments. Soft sessions are minimal (session id, route, invocation hash, creation_ts, ttl) to keep memory pressure low. Sessions are garbage-collected aggressively and emitted metrics track session hits/misses/evictions.
- SDK changes: Python/TS SDKs parse Retry-Sample and feed samples into an adaptive backoff policy that decays/bootstraps per-route. SDKs also expose a helper to automatically attach Idempotency-Grace on retry.
- Observability & safety: new metrics (route_retry_sample_emitted, soft_idempotency_hit, soft_idempotency_replay_rejected) and traces for session lifecycle. Gateways enforce a per-tenant emission limit for Retry-Sample to avoid amplification. Emitting the sample and creating a soft session are opt-in at route-level; default behavior enabled for most user-facing generation and tool routes.

Rollout plan:
- Canary on internal developer-facing routes for 48h.
- Gradual rollout to hosted API with feature flag by tenant for 2 weeks.
- Dedicated/Private will be off by default with operator opt-in and a persistent backend toggle.

Migration notes: consumers who rely on current static backoff parameters should update SDKs to pick up adaptive policy. Operators can disable Retry-Sample if they are concerned about exposing route-level congestion samples to clients.

Test plan: unit tests for header parsing/validation, integration tests simulating truncated streams and replays, flake-resistant timing tests for TTL behavior, and end-to-end SDK integration tests.

Security considerations: session IDs are opaque and short-lived; session acceptance checks for invocation hash to prevent replay of different payloads. We document the threat model and an operator knob to disable soft sessions. This PR bundles code, docs, tests, and a short migration guide.

review_thread: Diego Ramos: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) concrete example formats for Retry-Sample in the docs (show ms -> distribution), (2) ensure we never accept a replay that changes the invocation payload — how do we compute the invocation hash?

Mira Chen (author): Added explicit format examples to docs; invocation hash is SHA256 over canonicalized body+tool-id+user-id, described in docs and tests; added unit that verifies mismatched payloads are rejected.
Asha Patel: We should be conservative with the default TTL. Can we start with 15s for hosted and 45s for private? Also add a metric for sessions closed-by-ttl so we can monitor churn.
Mira Chen (author): Updated TTL defaults and added soft_idempotency_ttl_closed metric. Kept the feature flag so operators can tune per-deployment.
Lucas Nguyen: Integration tests flaky on first run (timing). Marked flake-resistant and added explicit clock control for session expiry. CI rerun looks good.
Diego Ramos: Approve after docs update. Asha Patel: Approve. Lucas Nguyen: Approve.
ci_summary: integration tests: initially flaky -> rerun -> pass
release_notes:
- Introduce Retry-Sample response header to help SDKs adapt client-side backoff heuristics per-route.
- Introduce Idempotency-Grace soft session to allow safe short-window replays for tool/function invocations, reducing failed duplicate invocations due to transient stream interruptions.
- SDKs updated with adaptive backoff helpers and automated attachment of Idempotency-Grace for retries.
Notes: feature is controlled by route-level flags and operator toggles; no breaking changes expected.
notes_for_ops: Default soft session TTLs: hosted=15s, private/dedicated=45s. Retry-Sample emission rate-limited per-route (1/30s). Operators can toggle soft sessions via runtime config: runtime.soft_idempotency.enabled=false. Persistent backend is optional for Dedicated/Private deployments.
